feedback.description: this memory records a correction somebody gave, and who gave it

memory.description: one thing a person said about how they want something built or handled, kept in their own words. The words themselves are the entity's doc.body, verbatim; these columns record where they belong and what is needed to read them. The byline is the entity's created{at, by}

space.description: whose space they were said in — every member of that space can read them, and they are deleted with it

about.description: the app they were said about, by slug, when they were about one

context.description: the line or two needed to understand the words — what was being talked about, never a restatement of what was said

memory_save.title: Keep what was said
memory_save.description: Keep somebody's words as they said them. The sentence itself is the memory — never your summary of it, which can only ever hold less — plus the line or two of context somebody needs to read it six weeks from now. scope names the project it belongs to; leave it out for a principle everybody carries. feedback names who GAVE the correction, when the words are one. Pass id instead to patch a memory that already exists: anything you leave out is left unchanged, and replacing the words requires was — the token memory recall returns beside them — so a memory another writer changed since you read it is rejected as a whole rather than overwritten.

said.description: the words the person used, as they used them

title.description: the index line a recall shows first

context.description: what was being talked about — two lines, never a restatement of what was said

scope.description: the project the words belong to; unsaid, they are everybody's

feedback.description: who GAVE the correction these words are — a person, or empty where nobody knows whose they were. Either way the memory is marked as feedback

about.description: the app they were said about, by slug

id.description: a memory to patch instead of creating one

was.description: the token memory recall printed for the words you are replacing

memory_recall.title: What was said about this
memory_recall.description: The memories nearest what you are doing. said is matched against their text as a PHRASE, so use the words you expect the memory to contain rather than a sentence of your own; near names an entity and ranks by MEANING instead, where this server keeps vectors, which is the ranking that answers a sentence; with neither, the newest are returned. Each is returned WHOLE — half of what somebody said is worse than none of it — carrying the $was token memory save requires before it replaces any of them.

said.description: the words you expect them to have used — matched as a phrase

near.description: an entity to rank by meaning, where this server keeps vectors

scope.description: only the ones filed under this project

feedback.description: only the ones recording a correction somebody gave
